title: Bounded acyclic flat models represent the proper coefficient map termwise
statement:
Let $r:W\to V$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small etale sites and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ and $\lambda:T_Wr_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}r_B^*T_V$ for the canonical tensor/pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define $q_r:T_VRr_{*,A}\to Rr_{*,B}T_W$ as the adjoint transpose under $r_B^*\dashv Rr_{*,B}$ of $T_W(\varepsilon_A)\circ\lambda^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon_A:r_A^*Rr_{*,A}\to1$ is the counit [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

Let $C$ be a cochain complex of $A_W$-module sheaves, zero outside a finite interval, and put $C_B=C\otimes_{A_W}B_W$ termwise. Assume each $C^n$ is flat over $A_W$, meaning tensoring with it is exact; assume each $r_{*,A}C^n$ is flat over $A_V$; and assume for every $n$ and every $a>0$ that
$$R^ar_{*,A}(C^n)=0,\qquad R^ar_{*,B}(C^n\otimes_{A_W}B_W)=0.$$
Then the canonical acyclic-complex comparison maps identify $Rr_{*,A}C$ and $Rr_{*,B}C_B$ with the degreewise complexes $r_{*,A}C$ and $r_{*,B}C_B$, respectively. The complexes $C$ and $r_{*,A}C$ are K-flat (tensoring them with any acyclic complex gives an acyclic total tensor complex). Under these specified identifications and the flat-model identifications for $T$, the named map $q_r(C)$ is represented by the termwise sheaf projection morphism
$$\pi_C:(r_{*,A}C)\otimes_{A_V}B_V\longrightarrow r_{*,B}(C\otimes_{A_W}B_W),$$
whose degree-$n$ morphism is adjoint to
$$r_B^*((r_{*,A}C^n)\otimes_{A_V}B_V)\cong(r_A^*r_{*,A}C^n)\otimes_{A_W}B_W
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{A,C^n}\otimes1}C^n\otimes_{A_W}B_W.$$
The identifications and this representation are natural in chain maps between complexes satisfying these hypotheses. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), proper coefficient transformation. Agent-stated bounded acyclic-flat model calculation of the counit transpose; the acyclic-complex computation itself is lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity clause (3).

proof.text: Put $D=r_{*,A}C$, $E=C_B$, $H=r_{*,B}E$, and let $Q$ denote the relevant derived localization. For $R=A,B$, the module categories on $W_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$ are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian] and have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The functors $r_{*,R}$ are additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $r_R^*$ is the exact module inverse image, left adjoint to $r_{*,R}$; its derived functor is therefore represented termwise. In particular the ordinary adjunction induces the adjunction on homotopy categories to which [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] applies. We always use its canonical derived adjunction, the one specified in the statement.

Both $C$ and $E$ vanish outside the given finite interval. Apply clause (3) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] to the identity quasi-isomorphism of $C$, with $v=r_{*,A}$, and separately to the identity of $E$, with $v=r_{*,B}$. The two acyclicity assumptions are precisely its hypotheses on their terms. Consequently the canonical comparisons
$$\alpha_A:QD\longrightarrow Rr_{*,A}(QC),\qquad \alpha_B:QH\longrightarrow Rr_{*,B}(QE)$$
induce isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf and hence are isomorphisms in the derived categories. These are the natural comparison transformations of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], not arbitrary isomorphisms with the same objects. All complexes here are bounded below, so their canonical bounded-below computations are also the K-injective computations in the ordinary unbounded category.

The bounded complexes $C$ and $D$ have flat terms by the two flatness assumptions. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] on $(W_{\mathrm{Et}},A_W)$ and $(V_{\mathrm{Et}},A_V)$ respectively: both are K-flat. Thus the construction of [def-kun-derived-tensor] computes $T_W(QC)$ by $QE$ and $T_V(QD)$ by $Q(D\otimes_{A_V}B_V)$, naturally in maps of these flat models. This construction resolves the first factor only; it makes no flatness assumption on the second factor $B_T$. For the $B_T$-module typing, view $T_T$ as derived module pullback for the identity topos equipped with $A_T\to B_T$: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] gives exactly these scalar-extension complexes in $D(B_T)$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat) and the construction of derived tensor

proof.text:
Let $e_C:r_A^*D\to C$ be the chain map whose components are the ordinary counits. In [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], set $F=r_{*,A}$, $G=r_A^*$, $K=C$, $M=D$, $s=1_C$, $t=1_D$ and $f=1_D:D\to r_{*,A}C$. Its representing cocone component $p_{1_C}$ is $\alpha_A$, and its cone component $u_{1_D}$ is the exact-pullback comparison $Lr_A^*(QD)\simeq Q(r_A^*D)$. Its displayed characterization of the hom bijection therefore says that $\alpha_A$ has adjunct $Q(e_C)$. Equivalently,
$$\varepsilon_{A,QC}\circ r_A^*(\alpha_A)=Q(e_C).$$
Here and below the canonical exact-pullback comparison is understood. This establishes the counit normalization for the specified acyclic comparison, rather than inferring it from the existence of an isomorphism $QD\simeq Rr_{*,A}QC$.

source.place: Tag 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), hom-bijection formula at identity denominators

proof.text:
Pullback carries $D$ to a flat-term K-flat complex by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus $T_W(Q(e_C))$ is represented by $e_C\otimes1:r_A^*D\otimes_{A_W}B_W\to E$, using the flat models of [def-kun-derived-tensor] and their naturality [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. At $QD$ the canonical comparison $\lambda^{-1}$ is represented by ordinary pullback/tensor reassociation
$$\rho_D:r_B^*(D\otimes_{A_V}B_V)\xrightarrow{\sim}(r_A^*D)\otimes_{A_W}B_W.$$
Indeed module pullback is inverse image followed by tensor over the pulled-back ring, and the identified constant rings in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] make both sides the same base-extended inverse-image complex. Reassociation sends each local tensor to the same local tensor, in each degree; it commutes with the differentials. This is the flat-model construction of the canonical comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Naturality of $\lambda$, followed by the equation of Step 4, shows that the adjunct of
$$q_r(QC)\circ T_V(\alpha_A)$$
is represented by the chain map
$$a=(e_C\otimes1)\rho_D:r_B^*(D\otimes_{A_V}B_V)\longrightarrow E.$$

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); ordinary pullback/tensor reassociation on flat models

proof.text:
The degree-$n$ adjunct under the ordinary $B$-module adjunction of $a^n$ is exactly the displayed morphism $\pi_C^n$ in the statement. These degreewise adjuncts form a chain map: naturality of the hom bijection applied to $d_C^n$ gives
$$r_{*,B}(d_E^n)\pi_C^n=\pi_C^{n+1}(d_D^n\otimes1).$$
Now apply the formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with $F=r_{*,B}$, $G=r_B^*$, $K=E$, $M=D\otimes_{A_V}B_V$, $s=1_E$, $t=1_M$ and $f=\pi_C$. The cocone component is $p_{1_E}=\alpha_B$, and exactness of $r_B^*$ again identifies $u_{1_M}$ with termwise pullback. The formula says precisely that
$$\alpha_B\circ Q(\pi_C):Q(D\otimes_{A_V}B_V)\longrightarrow Rr_{*,B}(QE)$$
has adjunct $Q(a)$. This application needs no flatness of $M$ as a $B_V$-complex, because $r_B^*$ itself is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

source.place: Tag 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), applied directly to the chain map pi_C

proof.text:
Steps 5 and 6 give the same adjunct. Injectivity of the hom bijection [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] implies
$$q_r(QC)\circ T_V(\alpha_A)=\alpha_B\circ Q(\pi_C).$$
Since the two $\alpha$ maps are the specified isomorphisms of Step 2, this equality is exactly the asserted representation of $q_r(C)$ under those identifications and the flat-model identifications of Step 3.

source.place: Tag 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), injectivity of the hom bijection

proof.text:
For a chain map $h:C\to C'$ between complexes in the statement, the maps $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$ commute with $h$ and $h\otimes1$ by naturality of the comparison in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The flat-model identifications commute with $h$ and $r_{*,A}h$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Naturality of the ordinary counit gives $h e_C=e_{C'}r_A^*(r_{*,A}h)$, and naturality of $\rho$ then gives $(h\otimes1)a_C=a_{C'}r_B^*((r_{*,A}h)\otimes1)$. Taking ordinary adjuncts yields
$$r_{*,B}(h\otimes1)\pi_C=\pi_{C'}((r_{*,A}h)\otimes1).$$
Thus the comparison equality of Step 7 and all its specified identifications are natural. Only boundedness, the two termwise flatness assumptions and the two acyclicity assumptions were used; no flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ enters.
